responsibilities: Understand HELE's vision, strategies, and organizational priorities.
Develop a deep understanding of customer needs.
Build/Propose solutions that enable data-driven decision-making within HELE.
Understand business models, data sources, system infrastructure.
Design and implement robust Power BI Architectures that empower organization-wide self-service reporting and ad-hoc data exploration.
Design and Implement a Power BI COE in partnership with key partners within different business departments and functions.
Apply a hands-on approach to build and lead the key analytical assets needed for the organization.
Develop scalable Power BI data models that drive strategic decision-making and deliver measurable business value.
Optimally delegate and use repartees and other individuals (consultants/onsite/offshore) and ensure accountability to delivering timely solutions.
Ensure solutions are adequately embraced and used by the business groups.
Ensure accountability with various partners who are contributing to building Power BI solutions.
Adoption and use of agile methodologies for all activities.
Design and implement proven methods for DevOps and project management including vital metrics and measures.
Incorporate proven methods for governing Power BI solutions including the use of a business glossary, standard KPI, business definitions, etc.
Guide and support team members and business users in building their own reports on top of scalable Power BI models.
Stay updated with the latest data trends and technologies to enhance our BI capabilities continuously.

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Incorporate proven methods for governing Power BI solutions including the use of a business glossary, standard KPI, business definitions
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Rigour: governance ('business glossary, standard KPI, business definitions'), robust architectures and accountability outweigh the single 'fast-paced environment'.
evidence.domain_risk: crafting analytical tools that drive decision-making at every level of the organization
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Moderate: internal BI for a consumer products company, where errors affect business decisions with no financial-reporting or regulatory language.
evidence.data_team_maturity: Design and Implement a Power BI COE in partnership with key partners within different business departments and functions
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: Mid: Power BI already runs 'as an enterprise platform' with consultants and offshore help, but the role must still set up the Power BI COE.
evidence.jd_authorship: Design and implement robust Power BI Architectures that empower organization-wide self-service reporting and ad-hoc data exploration
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Mixed: some precise Power BI bullets (COE, business glossary, scalable models) sit beside generic ones such as 'Develop a deep understanding of customer needs'.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: Internal data: the audience is the company's own report builders, through 'organization-wide self-service reporting' and guiding business users on shared models.
evidence.autonomy_level: Design and Implement a Power BI COE
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: Strategic: the role designs the BI architecture, sets up the 'Power BI COE' and will 'build and lead the key analytical assets'.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: No AI skill is expected of the candidate.
evidence.testing_framing: No testing or data quality signal.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Absent: governance appears as a business glossary and standard KPI definitions, with no testing, data quality or observability practice.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: None: the posting is framed in delivery and adoption terms, not risk.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Design and Implement a Power BI COE
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Greenfield: the dominant verbs are design and implement, for new Power BI architectures, a COE and DevOps methods.
